note: Group Content Moderation integrates core content_moderation with the group module by decorating two core services in a ServiceProvider: content_moderation.state_transition_validation (-> GroupStateTransitionValidation) and access_check.latest_revision (-> LatestRevisionCheck). It has NO settings form (configure=null). It provides GROUP permissions (gcontent_moderation.group.permissions.yml): a static 'view latest version' plus dynamic 'use <workflow_id> transition <transition_id>' generated by GroupContentModerationPermissions::groupPermissions() for every content_moderation workflow/transition. It ships an optional view moderated_group_content (page path group/%group/moderated) and a Views filter group_content_respect_unpublished. Medium/hard cases are grounded in real state: the dynamically generated group permissions for a content_moderation workflow created in setup, and the moderated_group_content view config. Scripts create/delete a namespaced workflow (gcmod_*) and restore the view's shipped pager value.

evals.prompt: How does the gcontent_moderation module make core Content Moderation workflow transitions respect a user's Group membership instead of only their global permissions?
evals.expected_output: It decorates core's content_moderation.state_transition_validation service (with GroupStateTransitionValidation) via a ServiceProvider, so valid transitions are filtered by the member's group permissions of the form 'use <workflow> transition <id>' in the current group's context.

evals.prompt: In gcontent_moderation, what is the naming pattern of the group permission that lets a group member perform a particular content-moderation transition, and what static group permission lets them see pending revisions?
evals.expected_output: Dynamic per-transition group permissions are named 'use <workflow_id> transition <transition_id>' (e.g. 'use editorial transition publish'), generated for every content_moderation workflow. The static permission 'view latest version' lets members view pending/latest revisions.

evals.prompt: What view/page does gcontent_moderation provide for reviewing a group's moderated content, at what path, and does the module have an admin settings form?
evals.expected_output: It ships the optional 'Moderated group content' view (moderated_group_content) with a page at group/%group/moderated, gated by the 'view latest version' group permission. The module has no settings form (configure=null).

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a Content Moderation workflow with machine name 'gcmod_editorial'. Given how gcontent_moderation generates group permissions, inspect the live workflow's transitions and give the exact group permission id that would let a group member run its 'publish' transition.
evals.expected_output: The group permission id is 'use gcmod_editorial transition publish' (pattern: use <workflow_id> transition <transition_id>). Inspect the gcmod_editorial workflow's transitions to confirm the 'publish' transition exists.

evals.prompt: On this site, inspect the 'Moderated group content' (moderated_group_content) view provided by gcontent_moderation and tell me how many items per page its pager is currently configured to show.
evals.expected_output: The moderated_group_content view's default-display pager items_per_page is 33. Read via drush cget views.view.moderated_group_content or entity storage.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site (gcontent_moderation is enabled), set up a Content Moderation workflow with machine name exactly 'gcmod_task' that includes a transition named 'publish' leading to a published state, so that gcontent_moderation exposes the group permission to use that transition. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A content_moderation workflow 'gcmod_task' with a 'publish' transition exists, so GroupContentModerationPermissions::groupPermissions() contains the key 'use gcmod_task transition publish'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure the 'Moderated group content' (moderated_group_content) view provided by gcontent_moderation so that its pager shows 25 items per page. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In views.view.moderated_group_content the default display pager options items_per_page is 25 (edit the view's pager and save).
